title: Ministries 1 of 4: a ministry and the directory
question: How a ministry looks to a visitor, a parent whose child attends, and a team member, and the directory of ministries. Underneath is the same for all three: four audiences (Everyone, Attendees and their parents, Parents only, Team only), nesting to any depth, roles through Access. Which should I build?

options.label: The bulletin board
options.thesis: Each area boxes what you can see by who it's for, team first.
options.viewport: Directory: Yours, serving teams, Life Groups. A ministry: header with its one action (Ask to join, Mia attends, On the team), then About, News, Calendar, Files; in News a box each for the team, families, parents and everyone.
options.risk: A box per audience adds a little height when a ministry posts to all four.

options.label: The family tree
options.lineage: an organisation chart folded into a list
options.thesis: The directory is the ministry tree itself; items carry a coloured audience word.
options.viewport: Directory as Music › Choir, Production… folding open; a ministry with a Teams tab, locked tabs showing what joining opens; News as one list with Team, Families, Parents words at each row's end.
options.risk: Buries 'where I go' under the structure; words at a row's end are easy to miss.

options.label: For you first
options.lineage: a reminder note on the fridge
options.thesis: Each ministry opens on what's next for you, then one list of what's new.
options.viewport: Directory leads with your next thing (Mia at Impact Kids, Friday 6:30pm); a ministry opens on 'For Mia · this Friday', then What's new with who each is for, Calendar, Files, About as chips.
options.risk: Lovely for a parent; leaders lose the areas as places.
